# Our data {background-color="#dc354a"}

## NHL player stats, 2023–24

```{.r .cell-code}
hockey = read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hbdaarstad/NHL-22-24-Season-Data/main/hockey_stats.csv") |>
```

## Team goals by position

This one is made for you: each team's total goals by position, plus a `Total` column



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
hockey_goals <- hockey |>
  group_by(team, position) |>
  summarise(goals = sum(goals, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = position, values_from = goals, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(-team)))

hockey_goals
```

# Box plots {background-color="#dc354a"}

## 🚨 Your turn: 🏒 Goals Box Plot 🏒 🚨

Using the `hockey` dataset:

1.  Build a box plot of the number of `goals` scored by all NHL players in the 2023–24 regular season.

2.  Color the outliers and change their shape.

3.  Add a point for the **mean** number of goals.

4.  Add a title, subtitle, and axis labels.

::: callout-tip
1.  Use `aes(x = "", y = goals)` to get a single box

2.  Outliers are set inside `geom_boxplot()` with `outlier.color =`, `outlier.shape =`, `outlier.size =`

3.  To add the mean: `stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point")`
:::



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}

```{=html}
<countdown-timer class="countdown" id="timer_29df885e" minutes="5" seconds="0" update-every="1" tabindex="0" style="right:0;bottom:0;"></countdown-timer>
```

:::
:::



## 🚨 🏒 Goals Box Plot Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}



::: {.cell layout-align="center" output-location='column'}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(data = hockey, aes(x = "", y = goals)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    alpha = 0.7,                       # transparency of the box fill
    outlier.color = "cornflowerblue",  # color of outlier points
    outlier.shape = 8,                 # outlier symbol is a star
    outlier.size = 1                   # outlier size
  ) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point",
               shape = 20, size = 4, color = "coral") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Regular Season Goals by Player",
       subtitle = "NHL 2023–24",
       x = "",
       y = "Goals Scored") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](lec-5_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%}
:::
:::



::: notes
The mean sits above the median: a few big scorers pull the mean up (right-skewed)
:::

## 🚨 Your turn: 🏒 Team Goals by Position 🏒 🚨

What **percent** of each team's goals comes from each position?

Using `hockey_goals`:

1.  Make a new object called `hockey_boxplot` with the percent of goals from each position: `rw_percent`, `lw_percent`, `c_percent`, `d_percent`.

2.  Make a box plot for each position and combine them with `patchwork`.

::: callout-tip
1.  Percent = the position's goals divided by `Total`, times 100. Use `mutate()`

2.  Combine plots with `+` and set the layout with `plot_layout(ncol = 4)`
:::



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}

```{=html}
<countdown-timer class="countdown" id="timer_6a74f971" minutes="7" seconds="0" update-every="1" tabindex="0" style="right:0;bottom:0;"></countdown-timer>
```

:::
:::



## 🚨 🏒 Team Goals by Position Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}

Step 1: the percentages



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
hockey_boxplot <- hockey_goals |>
  mutate(
    rw_percent = R / Total * 100,
    lw_percent = L / Total * 100,
    c_percent  = C / Total * 100,
    d_percent  = D / Total * 100
  )

hockey_boxplot
```

# Time series {background-color="#dc354a"}

## 🚨 Your turn: 🏒 Canadiens Searches 🏒 🚨

Using the `google_trends` dataset:

1.  Make a time series plot of the Google search score for the Montreal Canadiens (`montreal_canadiens`) by `month`, 2004 to 2026.

2.  Label the x-axis every 2 years.

3.  Add a trend line and a dashed line at the average score.

4.  Add a title, subtitle, axis labels, and a caption.

::: callout-tip
1.  Connect the points with `geom_line()`

2.  `scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y")`

3.  Trend line: `geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE)`. Average: `geom_hline(yintercept = mean(...), linetype = 2)`
:::



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}

```{=html}
<countdown-timer class="countdown" id="timer_b347bbff" minutes="6" seconds="30" update-every="1" tabindex="0" style="right:0;bottom:0;"></countdown-timer>
```

:::



## 🚨 🏒 Canadiens Searches Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}


# Creating a new variable {background-color="#dc354a"}

## 🚨 Your turn: 🏒 Playoff Teams 🏒 🚨

Using `hockey_boxplot` and the `playoffs_2024` list:

1.  Make a new variable called `playoffs` that is `"Clinched"` if the team made the playoffs and `"Eliminated"` if it did not.

2.  Store it as a new object called `hockey_newvar`.

::: callout-tip
1.  `case_when()` goes **inside** `mutate()`

2.  `%in%` checks whether a value is in a list: `team %in% playoffs_2024`

3.  There is no `!%in%`. For "not in", use `!(team %in% playoffs_2024)`
:::



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}

```{=html}
<countdown-timer class="countdown" id="timer_2b0c646a" minutes="4" seconds="0" update-every="1" tabindex="0" style="right:0;bottom:0;"></countdown-timer>
```

:::
:::



## 🚨 🏒 Playoff Teams Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
hockey_newvar <- hockey_boxplot |>
  mutate(playoffs = case_when(
    team %in% playoffs_2024 ~ "Clinched",
    !(team %in% playoffs_2024) ~ "Eliminated"
  ))

hockey_newvar |>
  select(team, Total, playoffs)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

# t-tests {background-color="#dc354a"}

## 🚨 Your turn: 🏒 t-test 🏒 🚨

Using `hockey_newvar`:

1.  Test whether teams that made the playoffs scored more **total goals** (`Total`) than teams that did not.

2.  Make a new variable `offense_perct`: the percent of goals from forwards (right wing + left wing + center).

3.  Test whether playoff teams get a different percent of their goals from **defense** (`d_percent`).

4.  Which differences are statistically significant?

::: callout-tip
1.  The formula is `t.test(OUTCOME ~ GROUP, data = DATA)`

2.  A difference is statistically significant if the **p-value** is less than 0.05
:::



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}

```{=html}
<countdown-timer class="countdown" id="timer_caa44998" minutes="6" seconds="30" update-every="1" tabindex="0" style="right:0;bottom:0;"></countdown-timer>
```

:::
:::



## 🚨 🏒 t-test Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}



::: {.cell layout-align="center" output-location='column'}

```{.r .cell-code}
t.test(Total ~ playoffs, data = hockey_newvar)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Welch Two Sample t-test

data:  Total by playoffs
t = 4.044, df = 28.598, p-value = 0.0003621
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Clinched and group Eliminated is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
 18.02924 54.97076
sample estimates:
  mean in group Clinched mean in group Eliminated 
                268.9375                 232.4375 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
hockey_ttest <- hockey_newvar |>
  mutate(offense_perct = rw_percent + lw_percent + c_percent)

t.test(d_percent ~ playoffs, data = hockey_ttest)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Welch Two Sample t-test

data:  d_percent by playoffs
t = -1.4916, df = 29.895, p-value = 0.1463
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Clinched and group Eliminated is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
 -4.2476960  0.6621946
sample estimates:
  mean in group Clinched mean in group Eliminated 
                13.41861                 15.21136 
```


:::
:::



. . .

**Total goals**: playoff teams scored about 269 goals vs. 232, p = 0.0004: **significant**

. . .

**Defense share**: p = 0.15: **not** significant

. . .

::: callout-note
`offense_perct` and `d_percent` always add up to 100, so testing `offense_perct` gives the same p-value
:::

        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
